answer: Backseat is a charity ride-sharing platform. If you're travelling alone, you can offer your spare seat to someone going the same way. They travel with you freely — and if they wish, they can donate any amount to registered charity partners. It's never a fare, always voluntary.

For riders: Register → Add your vehicle → Get verified → Offer your route → Show your Charity QR. For passengers: Search a route → Request to join → Travel together → Scan the rider's QR → Donate any amount if you wish. There is no fare — donations are always voluntary and go to charity.

Go to the Register page and fill in your full name (2-80 characters), email address, phone number (optional), and a password (minimum 8 characters). Email must be unique. After registration you'll be redirected to your dashboard.
Go to the Login page and enter your registered email and password. If your account is blocked, you'll need to contact support. There is no self-service password reset yet.

To offer a ride you need a rider profile. Go to Offer a Ride, set your starting point, destination, departure date/time, number of seats to share (1-6), and any notes. Your vehicle must be verified by an admin before your ride goes live. There is no fare field — rides are free.

Go to Become a Rider and fill in your vehicle details: type (two-wheeler or four-wheeler), make, model, registration plate, and number of spare seats (1-6). You can also add a short bio. After submission, an admin will verify your vehicle. Your charity QR stays inactive until verified.

Go to Find a Ride and search by pickup location, destination, and vehicle type (two-wheeler or four-wheeler). Browse results as ticket-style cards showing route, vehicle, seats, departure time, and rider verification badge. Click a ride to see details and send a join request.

When you find a ride, click Join to send a request. The rider will see your request and can Accept or Decline it. If accepted, you're confirmed for the ride. You'll receive a notification at each step. You can cancel your request anytime before it's accepted.

Go to Dashboard → My Trips to see all rides you've requested. Each trip shows the route, rider name, departure time, and status (Requested, Accepted, Declined, Completed, or Cancelled). For completed rides, you'll see a button to support the rider's charity.

Go to Dashboard → My Rides to see all rides you've offered. For active rides you can mark them completed or cancelled. For each join request you can Accept, Decline, or Mark as Travelled. After marking travelled, you can show your Charity QR inline for the passenger to scan.

After a ride, the passenger can scan the rider's charity QR code. On the donation page, choose an amount (suggested: ₹50, ₹100, ₹250, ₹500, or any custom amount up to ₹1,00,000). Tap 'Pay via UPI App' to open your UPI app, complete the payment, then confirm. You'll receive a receipt. Donations are entirely voluntary.

After a successful donation, you're redirected to a receipt page showing the amount, receipt ID, transaction ID, date, charity name, and status. You can download/print the receipt or share it via the share button.

Verified riders can access their Charity QR from Dashboard → QR. The QR code links to a donation page with the rider's unique charity code. Passengers scan this to donate. You can copy the link or regenerate a new code (old code stops working). The QR is only active after vehicle verification.

Backseat includes: verified rider profiles, vehicle verification by admins, SOS button (alerts all admins instantly and shows emergency number 112), report/block functionality, ride sharing options, and admin review workflows. Always check the rider's verification badge, share your trip details, meet in public, and trust your instincts.

Tap the SOS button (available on all pages). It's a two-step process: first tap opens a confirmation, second tap sends an alert to all admins with your current page context. After sending, you'll see a button to call 112 (India's national emergency number).

Go to the rider's public profile page and click Report. Choose a reason: Unsafe driving, Inappropriate behaviour, No-show, Fake profile, or Other. Add optional details (up to 500 characters). Reports are reviewed by admins. You cannot report yourself.

Go to the rider's public profile page and click Block. This prevents you from seeing their rides in search results and vice versa. You cannot block yourself. Admins can also block users from the admin portal.

When a ride request is in Requested, Accepted, or Completed status, you can chat with the other party directly from My Trips (for passengers) or My Rides (for riders). Messages are limited to 500 characters each. The chat refreshes automatically every 6 seconds.

The leaderboard shows the top 50 riders ranked by total donations received through their charity QR. You can choose how your name appears: full name, first name + initial, or completely anonymous ('A kind traveller'). Riders can also hide themselves from the leaderboard. Donations are voluntary — riders never see this as a target.

Go to Dashboard → Profile. You can edit your name, phone number, and leaderboard display preference. Three options: Show full name, Show first name + last initial (e.g. 'Ravi K.'), or Show as 'A kind traveller' (anonymous). You can also update your vehicle seats and bio if you're a rider.

After login, your dashboard shows an overview based on your role. Passengers see rides joined and total donated. Riders see a full stats grid: rides offered, people helped, total donations, charity impact, active ride status, and leaderboard rank. It also has quick links to My Rides, Donations, Impact, Profile, and buttons to Offer a Ride or view your Charity QR.

Go to Dashboard → Payments. It shows both sides: donations you made as a passenger, and donations received through your charity QR as a rider. Every rupee goes straight to the registered charity partner's account. A rider never receives money directly.

Your personal impact page (Dashboard → Impact) shows donations grouped by campaign with descriptions and amounts. The public Charity Impact page shows platform-wide totals: total collected, total distributed, and total beneficiaries supported. 100% of donations go to registered charity partners.

Backseat rides are not fare-based. A rider offers an empty seat for free, and a passenger may optionally donate any amount to charity after the ride. Riders never set, request, or receive any payment. All donations go directly to registered charity partners.

100% of donations go to our registered charity partners' bank accounts via UPI. Riders never receive money directly. The charity's UPI ID is configured by platform admins — riders cannot change or see it. Every transaction has a unique reference number for transparency.

Donations are voluntary charitable contributions. They are not automatically eligible for tax deduction unless the receipt explicitly states otherwise. Contact the specific charity for tax exemption details.
The maximum single donation is ₹1,00,000. For amounts higher than this, please contact the charity directly. There is no minimum amount — you can donate any positive number you choose.

Backseat supports two vehicle types: Two Wheeler (bike/motorcycle) and Four Wheeler (car). When you register as a rider, you provide vehicle make, model, and registration plate. An admin will verify your vehicle before your charity QR goes live. To change plate, make, or model, you'll need to contact support for re-verification.
You can offer between 1 and 6 spare seats per ride. When creating a ride, you choose how many seats to share from your available pool. Passengers cannot join once all seats are filled.

When offering a ride, you set a departure date and time using the date-time picker. The departure must be in the future (defaults to 30 minutes from now). In Find a Ride, only future departures are shown. If a ride has already departed, passengers can no longer join.

Passengers can cancel their join request anytime before the rider accepts it. Riders can cancel an entire active ride from My Rides (this cancels all pending requests). Once a ride is marked Completed, it cannot be cancelled.

Riders can mark individual join requests as 'Travelled' once the passenger has boarded. The overall ride offer can be marked 'Completed' from My Rides. After completion, the passenger sees a prompt to support the rider's charity via the QR code.

The admin portal (accessible to admin accounts only) provides: Overview stats, User management (block/unblock), Rider & vehicle verification, Ride management, Donation tracking, Charity & campaign management, Fraud detection, Leaderboard management, Reports review, and Audit logs.

The platform automatically flags suspicious activity for admin review: High-value donations (₹20,000+) and rapid repeat donations (3+ from same person to same rider within 1 hour). These are informational flags — no accounts are auto-blocked. Admins review and act manually.

The notification bell in the navigation bar shows unread notification count. You get notifications for: ride requests, acceptances, declines, completions, new chat messages, donation confirmations, and SOS alerts. Tap any notification to go to the relevant page. Use 'Mark all read' to clear the badge.

Backseat partners with registered charities. The charity's name, description, and registration number are shown on the Charity Impact page. Donations go directly to the charity's registered UPI account. Riders cannot see or change where the money goes.

Backseat community guidelines: No fares ever (riders cannot set/request payment), donations are always voluntary, be honest in your profile, treat every journey with respect, and report what doesn't feel right. Violations can result in warnings, suspension, or permanent removal.
Backseat has Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and Disclaimers pages accessible from the footer. These cover data handling, liability limitations, and platform rules.
Backseat is built by VitalitySoft. It's a charity ride-sharing movement aimed at making every journey count by connecting people who share the same route.

You can add a phone number during registration or later from your Profile page. Phone format: 10-15 digits with optional + prefix. Email and phone must be unique across the platform. Verification badges appear on your profile once verified by an admin.

Each rider has a public profile showing: name, verification badge, contributor rank, bio, stats (charity rides, donations generated, member since), vehicle info, and currently active ride offers. You can also report or block the rider from this page.

From Dashboard → QR, you can regenerate your charity QR code. This creates a new unique charity code and your old QR stops working. You'll be asked to confirm before regenerating. Use this if you want a fresh link.

When donating, tap 'Pay via UPI App' to open your default UPI app (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm, etc.) with the payment details pre-filled. Complete the payment in your UPI app, then come back and tap 'I've completed this payment' to confirm. The charity's UPI ID is used — never the rider's.

As a rider, you can toggle your sharing status ON/OFF from the Offer a Ride page. When OFF, your rides don't appear in search results for new passengers. Existing join requests are not affected. Your sharing turns ON automatically when you create a ride.

The homepage and dashboard display real-time platform statistics: total amount donated, total charity rides shared, people helped (distinct passengers), active riders, monthly contributors, and lifetime contributors. All stats exclude failed and refunded donations.

Demo accounts for testing: Admin (admin@backseat.app / Admin@123), Demo Rider (demo.rider@backseat.app / Demo@123), Demo Passenger (demo.passenger@backseat.app / Demo@123). Pre-seeded ride routes include Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, and Chennai.

Backseat is NOT a taxi or ride-hailing service. There are no fares, no pricing, no surge charges, no driver earnings. It's a charity movement — riders share seats voluntarily, and passengers donate to charity if they choose. The platform never charges anyone.

Go to Dashboard → Profile. Under the Vehicle section (for riders), you can update your spare seats (1-6) and bio (max 280 characters). To change your vehicle plate, make, or model, you'll need to contact support for re-verification.

When searching for rides, results are limited to 30 per page. Only rides from verified riders with active sharing are shown. Each ride card displays the route, vehicle type, seats available, departure time, rider name, and verification status.
